alex: quick q — seeing a handful of 500s from a customer. They provided X-Request-Id: 8f3a2c1b. Console search for that id returns nothing. Where should I look? Any tips for console vs CLI?

jamie: console's search index sometimes strips short ids. Try searching the full header name `x-rdw-request-id:8f3a2c1b` and also the bare id `8f3a2c1b`.
Also open Console → Observability → Traces and paste a suspected trace id if you have one. Traces often link back to logs via span tags.

alex: I only have the request id, no trace id. Edge proxy might rewrite the header — how do I map req id -> trace id?

ben: quick cheatsheet i use: `stern -n production 'edge-proxy|api' --since 15m | rg "8f3a2c1b" -n` to eyeball where it shows up. Edge can rename it to `x-rdw-request-id`. If you find it in edge logs you'll often see a span/trace link in the same line.
If console search misses it, try the raw ingress logs: `kubectl logs deploy/nginx-ingress -n production --since=30m | rg 8f3a2c1b`

jamie: internal CLI trick — we have `redwoodctl traces fetch --query "tags.request_id:8f3a2c1b" --output json` which will return any matching trace/span. Then `redwoodctl traces describe <trace-id>` to open the span list. Example: `redwoodctl traces fetch --query 'tags.request_id:8f3a2c1b' | jq '.[0].trace_id'`

alex: running stern now, thanks.

ops-bot: Deploy note: prod deploy finished @21:10 — if errors started after that, might be related :gear:

alex: stern shows the edge-proxy line: `WARN edge-proxy request failed upstream=backend-12 status=502 x-rdw-request-id=8f3a2c1b span=4fae3b7c...` — found a span id! chasing upstream pod logs now.

ben: once you have the pod name, tail its app container: `kubectl logs -f pod/backend-12 -n production -c app --since=30m | rg "8f3a2c1b"` — that should reveal the 502 cause. Also check Sentry / error-trace for that span id.

alex: found backend timeout to embeddings service, correlated with span 4fae3b7c — filing a small revert/rollout. closing the loop, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
